summary: Washington County, MD tower at Sideling Hill, planned in a 1930 state program; FFLA lists it standing with its cab in place. No build date, staffing or fire record found.

facts.agency: Maryland State Forestry Department (1930 program; tower status unconfirmed)

events.note: Proposed in the State Forestry Department's program of a dozen towers (article of 26 September 1930); the article does not confirm it was built

evidence.supports: 1930 program to build a dozen new fire towers, one planned at Sideling Hill in Washington County
evidence.quote: Included in the program of the State Forestry Department to build a dozen new fire towers throughout Maryland is one to be erected at Sideling Hill, this county.

evidence.supports: each tower to cost $1,500 to $2,000, funded by residents and timber owners, with no State appropriation
evidence.quote: each of the towers will cost between $1,500 to $2,000 with the funds to be raised through cooperation of residents and timber owners of the sections to be protected by each, no State appropriation being available for the work.

evidence.supports: the construction was to continue for six years
evidence.quote: The construction will continue through the next six years.

evidence.supports: the first tower was to be erected at Springfield in Prince George's County
evidence.quote: with the erection of the first tower at Springfield in Prince Georges county.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Sideling as a standing tower
FFLA legend: an asterisk marks towers whose cab is no longer in place
evidence.quote: Towers that retain their structure and support with the cab no longer in place are denoted as

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. The 1930 article is a plan, and nothing read confirms that the tower was built, its height, its cab, or who staffed it. FFLA lists it standing with no asterisk, so the cab is presumed in place. The 2007 Maryland DNR Forestry Towers report (https://dnr.maryland.gov/forests/documents/fire/Fire_Tower_Report.pdf) covers towers the state managed as of December 2006 and does not list a Sideling tower, so the tower may be privately or locally owned, or may be gone. The Wikipedia Sideling Hill article has no tower mention. Next steps: a Washington County or Maryland Forest Service archive search for the build date, and a newspaper search for the 1930s-40s. Access left unset because nothing was found.
